design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (ssl_certificate_lifecycle, env_0076) — rework round 3

DRAW (draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[5,4]. Root ssl_ext_install_charge takes 5 factors, prerequisite ssl_ext_support_renewal takes 4.

WHY A GOOD TEST. Dana Lindqvist asks Harborline support to install her DV Multi-Domain certificate on a second server her firm rents elsewhere. The installation rule's sentence 'A managed installation charge on a subscription inside its renewal window is not fixed until the subscription has been renewed past that window.' is unmet: the subscription ends 2026-12-18, 31 days away, auto-renew off. The agent must book a one-year support renewal (quoted with the early-renewal percentage off the certificate price only, the extra names unreduced, because it is booked more than 30 days before the end, plus the managed re-installation fee for the first server, less the Harborline Mail and Harborline DNS credits) and then the managed installation, which covers the current certificate and the automatic reissues the CA/B schedule (200-day certificates before 15 March 2027, 100-day after, reissue 30 days before expiry) puts on the server before the renewed end, at the repeat-installation rate, less the mail, same-day-renewal and DNS check credits. Both payments are made by the holder at checkout because her stored card expired (owner ruling (b)).

SCOPE. Task 0 claims ssl_ext_support_renewal (renew_certificate_subscription_0365c0e5, owner=user checkout) and ssl_ext_install_charge (pay_certificate_installation_15b30562, owner=user checkout). Task 1 claims the auto-renew, the complimentary names, the added name and the second-key order with their own tools; scopes are disjoint and cover all six policies.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Edge install -> support renewal, value_input, gate certs_covered, action form; fallback_reason: both the support renewal and the auto-renew move the end date, so the end-date state does not single out one write; auto-renew is off here, so the support renewal applies. Four-point test: negated direction ('not fixed until'), the waited-on side is the action 'renewed past that window', no tool/id/code token, scoped to subscriptions inside their renewal window. Unresolved: ssl_holdings end 2026-12-18, no renewal line. Skipping the renewal gives an installation of one certificate with no renewal bundle (9.99) instead of 67.47.

FACTOR CARD — support renewal (4): discount_family_ren method (tier schedule vs early-renewal promotion, single higher; Business Account gives none, booked 31 > 30 days ahead -> promotion only: price_1yr less 15 percent, extra names unreduced, 222.37; baseline none -> 234.87); mail_bundle_ren parameter email (Harborline Mail Plus -> 4.00; 231.37); dns_bundle_ren parameter domain (harborline_dns -> 3.00; 230.37); managed_reinst_ren parameter history (one installation line -> 12.00; 215.37). All-baseline 229.87.
FACTOR CARD — managed installation (5): reissue_cover_mi method (dns_cname -> 5 certificates; baseline 1 -> 7.49); repeat_rate_mi parameter history (one earlier installation -> 60 percent; 117.45); mail_bundle_mi parameter email (3.00; 70.47); renew_bundle_mi parameter history (renewal line billed today -> 2.50; 69.97); dns_check_mi parameter domain (2.00; 69.47). All-baseline 24.99.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. ssl_renewal.renew_active (status active); renewal window: bought from renewal_early_days = 90 days before the end; 2026-11-17 is 31 days before 2026-12-18 (inside). ssl_installation.install_active (active). Overwrites: ssl_renewal 'A renewal extends ...' and 'It is billed at ...' (scoped to support renewals; sibling tail names the auto-renew rule; base content restated); ssl_installation fee sentence (managed installation; hosting-plan rule restated). Account charter: the tier discount acts only on the renewal list price; no tier discount on the installation.

WORLD ROWS. customers (business profile, card ending 3471 expired per the persona); account (Harborline Business Account, no credit); domain northbankledger.com on Harborline DNS with registration and five auto-renews; Harborline Mail Plus subscription (domain_id = the domain) with purchase and auto-renew; ssl holding; purchase line 229.87 and managed installation 44.98 (priced under this charter's installation rule as of 2025-12-19); 3 ssl events.

PERSONA. Brisk partner; volunteers only the installation request and the second rented server; gives identity on request; states the stored card expired and that she pays at checkout with a new card (the in-person necessity); agrees to the renewal once explained; completes each checkout handed to her; ends after confirmation.

TRAPS. Pricing the installation before the renewal; using the tier schedule (none for a Business Account) instead of the early-renewal promotion; counting reissues with 100-day certificates before 15 March 2027 or with a 200-day cycle after it; missing the repeat rate or the same-day renewal bundle; charging the expired stored card.

VERIFICATION (scratch evaluator over the gate DSL): renewal 227.37 on the opening world; installation 67.47 after the renewal (9.99 without it); sensitivities as listed; the seeded 2025-12-19 installation recomputes to 44.98 under the installation rule.
user_scenario:
You are Dana Lindqvist, managing partner at Northbank Ledger Partners LLC in Dallas. You are calling Harborline because your firm has added a second web server for its client portal, rented from another hosting company and running alongside the first one, and you want Harborline's support team to install your multi-domain certificate for northbankledger.com on that new server for you, the way they installed it on the first one. You speak briskly and practically and think of this as one job for the support team.
You give your name and say you are calling about the certificate for northbankledger.com. When the agent asks you to confirm who you are, you offer the account email, dana@northbankledger.com, and, if a second detail is needed, your support PIN, 318204. Only if asked for something else do you add the phone number on the account, 2145550142. You never read out any account or record numbers; you do not know them.
If the agent asks about the new server, it is a server you rent from another hosting company, not a Harborline plan, and it serves exactly the names the certificate already covers. About payment: the company card on file, the one ending in 3471, expired last month and you have not replaced it on the account yet, so you will pay anything today yourself by entering the firm's new card at Harborline's checkout; you do not want account credit used. You have no idea what anything will cost and you do not volunteer any figure.
If the agent tells you that something has to be done to the existing certificate before the installation can be booked and explains what it is, you listen, and if it is a charge for the existing certificate you say that is fine. Whenever the agent hands you a payment to complete at checkout, you complete it yourself straight away exactly as the agent sets it out, entering the new card, and you read back the amount you see. If the agent gives you a figure that is plainly different from the one you just saw, you say so and ask them to check it against the record. Once the installation is paid and the agent confirms it is booked, you thank them and end the call; you do not ask for anything else.

edges.condition: The subscription_end_date lies more than renewal_early_days days after today, carried by a renewal line whose period_start is the end date it had before.
edges.policy_source: A managed installation charge on a subscription inside its renewal window is not fixed until the subscription has been renewed past that window.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: On 2026-11-17 the subscription ends 2026-12-18, 31 days away and inside the 90-day renewal window, with no renewal line and auto-renew off.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The support renewal writes a renewal line for 2026-12-18 to 2027-12-18 and sets the end date to 2027-12-18, 396 days away; the certificates covered rise from 1 to 5 and the renewal bundle credit applies.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Single edge; the installation reads the end date and the renewal line the renewal writes, and its rule states 'A managed installation charge on a subscription inside its renewal window is not fixed until the subscription has been renewed past that window.'

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the renewal the installation covers 1 certificate with no renewal bundle and comes to 9.99 instead of 67.47; the renewal line and the end date 2027-12-18 are missing.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only for the installation on the new server; it never mentions renewing, the end date or a renewal window. The customer agrees to a charge on the existing certificate only after the agent explains it.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: pay_certificate_installation_15b30562 and renew_certificate_subscription_0365c0e5 check only the amount, the checkout method and that the subscription exists; neither reads the end date or any renewal.
